summary.headline: Jain Irrigation Q1 FY27 revenue fell about 2.5% to Rs 1,500 crore; adjusted PAT dropped to Rs 3 crore from Rs 30 crore, with Rs 680 crore NCDs due this fiscal.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was about Rs 1,500 crore, down roughly 2.5% YoY, with Hi-Tech degrowing, Plastics flat and Agro-Processing growing on beverages and overseas sales. EBITDA fell because standalone India volumes were lower and fixed costs went unabsorbed; Hi-Tech margin fell to 14.4% from 16.6%. Management said April was weak, May-June improved, and July was positive, and it expects a stronger second half. Working capital days improved (consolidated net working capital 183 days vs 210 a year ago) and about 78% of EBITDA converted to cash.

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted PAT (after non-cash NCD interest unwinding)

financial_highlights.change: from 210 days in June 2025 and 186 days in March 2026

segments.name: Hi-Tech
segments.commentary: Revenue fell about 22% YoY; retail (MIS drip, tissue culture, solar) fell about 17% and projects fell about 63%. Drip (MIS) fell 16% from Rs 438 crore to Rs 368 crore; tissue culture fell 10%.

segments.name: Plastics
segments.commentary: Revenue roughly flat YoY; overseas plastics revenue grew about 40%, and segment EBITDA margin rose to about 11% from 10%.

segments.name: Agro-Processing (food)
segments.commentary: Grew significantly on new beverage business (about Rs 60 crore in April-June) and overseas sales, but EBITDA fell about 3 points on seasonality.

guidance_outlook: Management expects EBITDA lost in Q1 to be recovered in H2 FY27 and full-year PAT to beat FY26.
Hi-Tech: double-digit revenue growth targeted for FY27; solar pump sales expected to pick up from September.
FY27 margin guidance: about 14% standalone and about 12-13% consolidated.

Debt: about Rs 680 crore of NCDs due in FY27, about Rs 230 crore in September 2026 and the rest in March 2027; management says internal cash flows will cover them, with refinancing term sheets in hand.
Legacy government receivables target for FY27 is Rs 422 crore (minimum Rs 380 crore for the remaining nine months); Rs 60 crore collected in Q1 and Rs 25-30 crore in July.
Food business IPO deferred; management says it will look at it from September if markets improve.
capex_capacity: Biochar plant recently started (mango stones, corn cob, cotton stalk feedstock); management expects financial impact from next fiscal, with carbon credits taking 6-9 months.
Tamil Nadu land monetisation delayed by elections; management hopes it will be delivered in the current quarter.
Remaining project billing outside Pune is about Rs 40-50 crore; the large Pune water-supply project still has triple-digit crore billing left; Q2 project billing could be below Rs 24 crore.
demand_pricing: Polymer prices rose about 50%; most increases were passed to customers, and some customers postponed purchases until prices fall.
Delayed monsoon onset in June pushed drip sales into the current quarter; July was positive and August-September are expected to be good.
Government-linked and subsidy-driven micro-irrigation sales were deliberately not pursued because of cash flow and long receivables; management estimated Rs 50-60 crore of sales were forgone.
Dam storage was about 67% of capacity; management expects about 85% by monsoon-end, supportive of the rabi season and next summer.

qa_highlights.question: How much legacy government receivables were recovered and how much project work is left?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 60 crore received in Q1 and Rs 25-30 crore in July. Remaining project billing outside Pune is about Rs 40-50 crore, with no working capital needed; about 10-12 of 72 projects carry O&M over two to three years, which management called light.

qa_highlights.question: How will the Rs 674-680 crore of debt due this fiscal be repaid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited internal accruals first, then legacy receivable collections, asset monetisation (surplus land) and refinancing; it said Rs 1,300 crore of bank debt was repaid over three and a half years and that the company has never missed a payment in four years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Hi-Tech down about 22% and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail fell about 17% and projects about 63%; management called the drip decline a one-off from the delayed monsoon and polymer-driven postponements. Hi-Tech margin was 14.4% vs 16.6%, and management expects margins to recover to typical levels through the year.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk of write-offs on project receivables?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said provisions were made in FY21-22 after a project review and it does not expect material write-offs; net receivables of Rs 1,975 crore in June are largely good, with about 55% linked to government-related items.

qa_highlights.question: Why are working capital requirements higher than listed peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to legacy long-term project receivables and state-government orders paid after 6-12 months, and said the cycle should improve substantially in FY28 once project receivables are cleared.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of refinancing and the food-business IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no pushback from lenders, a couple of term sheets are in hand, and talks are ongoing. The food-business IPO (about Rs 1,000 crore including PE exit) has been deferred due to weak valuations; the company will revisit it from September.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PAT negative when revenue is flat, and what are the coffee and biochar updates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the loss to higher raw-material costs and lower standalone India volumes, and expects a full-year PAT improvement. First coffee orders have come from the Coffee Board; the biochar business has started, with impact on numbers from next fiscal.

risks_watch: Refinancing of about Rs 230 crore NCD due in September 2026 and about Rs 450 crore due in March 2027 has not yet been completed; management relies on term sheets and internal cash flows.
Legacy government receivables of about Rs 800-900 crore and about Rs 500 crore of agency receivables above 180 days; collection pace against the Rs 380 crore minimum target is key.
Polymer price volatility and geopolitical oil-price movements may keep customers postponing purchases.
Weak Q1 adjusted PAT (Rs 3 crore) and reliance on H2 recovery; Q2 is seasonally muted.
Food-business IPO and Tamil Nadu land monetisation timelines have slipped repeatedly.
summary.management_tone: Confident on debt repayment and H2 recovery, but cautious on near-term volumes: Q1 is described as muted and beyond management's control. Answers on receivables and monetisation timelines were broad, and several timelines (Tamil Nadu land, IPO) were pushed out.
